clue.text: Considers food shop reprimands

parts.note: a deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling prepared foods
to berate someone is to scold or reprimand them

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about the telling-offs handed out at a delicatessen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Considers' reads as a plain verb opening a sentence, but it is the definition; the rest is a two-piece charade.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to weigh something up carefully, a synonym for considering it.

clue.text: Test cut back at Minehead

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for cut from right to left

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it

indicators.note: the head of the word Mine means its opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: An examination is reduced at a seaside town in Somerset.
explanation.walkthrough: Minehead is a seaside town in Somerset, England, but the clue splits it into 'Mine' and 'head'. 'back' turns AXE into EXA, and 'head' takes the M from 'Mine'.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test of knowledge.

clue.text: Again is covering such angers

indicators.note: covering means the word is wraps around the other piece

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Repetition covers up a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts IS around RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for anger or wrath, used here in the plural.

clue.text: Lands with a few cars

definitions.meaning: large areas of land owned by one person or family
estate cars have a long body with a rear door

explanation.surface: Someone owns property along with a small fleet of vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Large landed properties and station-wagon style vehicles share the same name.

clue.text: Ones that are champions

definitions.meaning: in a pack of playing cards, the ace is the card of value one
an ace is an expert or star performer

explanation.surface: A question of who counts as the winners.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing cards worth one share their name with expert performers.

clue.text: One finally died with wife, we left enlightened

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word One
with here means the word died holds the trimmed piece inside it
left means the letters of we have been taken away from wife

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grieving pair say that once one partner died, they were spiritually improved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E from 'One'; 'we left' strips W and E from WIFE to leave IF, which 'with' puts inside DIED to give DIFIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be edified is to be morally or intellectually improved, which is to be enlightened.

clue.text: One doesn't like people mixed in metaphors

indicators.note: mixed suggests the letters of in metaphors are jumbled, playing on mixed metaphors

explanation.surface: A grumpy figure turns up amid a muddle of figures of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the phrase 'mixed metaphors', but 'mixed' signals rearranging the eleven letters of IN METAPHORS.
explanation.definitionFit: A misanthrope is someone who dislikes or distrusts humankind in general.

clue.text: Singer — she's from France — into edible fungus

parts.note: a chanter is one who chants or sings
elle is the French word for she

explanation.surface: A French woman singer gets involved with mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is a link: the singer leads into the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: The chanterelle is a yellow, funnel-shaped wild mushroom prized for eating.

clue.text: Beauty that is in the outer depth

indicators.note: in places the word is between the two outer letters
the outer points to the first and last letters of depth

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lovely person, in some deep, far-off place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is a link; 'the outer' takes D and H from 'depth', and 'in' places IS between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is informal slang for an attractive person.

clue.text: He is upset in father and mother's rhetorical digression

indicators.note: in means the jumbled pair of words goes inside the word for mother and father

parts.note: a father and mother together are parents

indicators.note: upset means the letters of He is are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy is distressed by his parents' long-winded speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges HE IS to HESI, which 'in' places between PARENT and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A parenthesis is an aside or explanatory remark inserted into a passage, interrupting its flow.

clue.text: Legislation Norwegian capital has on linen

parts.note: law is legislation

indicators.note: capital means the capital, or opening letter, of Norwegian

explanation.surface: Oslo-style legislation applies to bed sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norwegian capital' wants to be Oslo, but it is just the first letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn is a fine, sheer linen or cotton fabric.

clue.text: Reputation jokers have on how to pay for goods

parts.note: credit is good standing or reputation
a card is a joker, a comic person; jokers are also playing cards

explanation.surface: Funny people with good standing explain how to settle up at a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have on' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic payment cards let a shopper buy now and settle the bill later.

clue.text: Clue: "antelopes get right in the backwoods"

parts.note: a hint is a clue

indicators.note: get right in means the abbreviation for right goes inside the word for the antelopes

parts.note: elands are large African antelopes

explanation.surface: A crossword clue about antelopes heading into remote country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' is a link; 'in' puts R inside ELANDS, giving ERLANDS after HINT.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinterland is the remote, thinly populated area far from the coast or cities.

clue.text: One in a list of names to celebrate

indicators.note: in means the numeral for one goes inside the word for a list of names

parts.note: a roster is a list of people's names, often for duties
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone finds their name on a duty roster and wants to party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside ROSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily, which is a boisterous way to celebrate.

clue.text: Capitalist from the manor

indicators.note: from here signals that the answer is made out of the letters of manor, rearranged

explanation.surface: A moneyed businessman comes from the big country house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitalist' suggests a business tycoon, but it means a person from a capital city, here Rome; 'from' tells us to make the answer out of the letters of MANOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Rome lives in Italy's capital, so is jokingly a capital-ist.

clue.text: Will it go to one who may stage a support

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball

explanation.surface: A question of whether a will benefits someone who might put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is the testament, not the verb; 'who may' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is a person who receives a legacy, so a dead person's will goes to them.

clue.text: Leans on the tables

definitions.meaning: a ship ... when it leans to one side

explanation.surface: Someone props themself against some furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's tilt to one side and a written catalogue of items share the same word.

clue.text: Flogged with one uninterrupted

indicators.note: with means the numeral for one is carried within the word for flogged

parts.note: flog is informal for sell, so flogged means sold
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone was whipped along with another person, without a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogged' looks like whipping, but it is slang for sold; 'with' places I inside SOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A solid stretch of time is continuous, with no gaps or breaks.

clue.text: A touch about such information

indicators.note: about means the letter A and the word for a touch are turned round together

parts.note: a tad is a touch, a small amount

explanation.surface: A small hint concerning that particular kind of knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses A plus TAD to give DATA, which is what the definition 'information' needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures, a form of information.

clue.text: Beholding gunner on the Scottish hillside

indicators.note: holding means the two letters of Be enclose the gunner's abbreviation

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for gunners

explanation.surface: Someone sees an artillery man up on a slope in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beholding' splits into 'Be' and 'holding': BE wraps around RA, the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Brae is a Scots word for a hillside or slope.

clue.text: Worker in pigs skin trousers

indicators.note: in means the insect goes between the two letters taken from pigs
skin points to the outside letters of pigs, its first and last

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A labourer wears trousers made of pigskin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pigs skin' looks like leather, but 'skin' takes P and S from 'pigs'; 'in' puts ANT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pants is the American and informal word for trousers.

clue.text: Sack bell-hop for taking ill

indicators.note: taking means the word for a bell-hop takes in ill

parts.note: a page or bell-hop runs errands in a hotel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hotel porter is dismissed for being off sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like dismiss, but means plunder; 'for' is a link and 'taking' puts ILL inside PAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to loot it violently, which is what pillaging means.

clue.text: Mark many east enders in red

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number

indicators.note: enders points to the end letters of east, its first and last

explanation.surface: A scar marks out lots of Londoners from the East End dressed in red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'east enders' evokes London's East End (and the TV soap EastEnders), but 'enders' takes E and T from 'east'. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a bright shade of red.

clue.text: Ground the queen into the coach

indicators.note: into means the queen's letters go inside the word for coach

parts.note: to coach someone is to train them
ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch is put on board the carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts ER inside TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land considered by its physical features, as ground.

clue.text: Apache trophy held centrally with knife

parts.note: a scalp was taken as a war trophy in tales of Apache warriors

indicators.note: centrally means the middle two letters of held are taken

explanation.surface: A grisly war trophy is taken with a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrally' takes EL from 'held'; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is a small, very sharp surgical knife.

clue.text: Promotion over mother having first son

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a promotion

indicators.note: over means the word for mother is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: ma is mother

explanation.surface: Mum's advertising campaign has her firstborn boy in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link; 'over' turns MA into AM.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, the first man was made by God, so is in a sense God's first son.

clue.text: Flick at the coat

definitions.meaning: a flick is informal for a movie

explanation.surface: Someone flicks dust off a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A movie and a thin covering layer share one word.

clue.text: Be after a get back situation to help

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Be after a get back situation to help' (4) for ABET, gives A + BE, but nothing in 'get back situation' fairly supplies the final T; the clue looks garbled.
annotationWithheld.clue: Be after a get back situation to help

clue.text: Drop round for pudding

parts.note: to sag is to droop or drop
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone drops by for dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch from palm pith, cooked with milk into a pudding.

clue.text: Brief advantage of one all over ban over English flavouring pod

parts.note: van is the short form of advantage in tennis scoring
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: over after all means that word is turned over and read backwards
the second over means the word ban sits over, or around, the letter for English

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddled account of a tennis score and a ban, ending in a pod used to flavour food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. The first 'over' turns ALL into LLA; the second 'over' wraps BAN around E to give BEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The cured seed pod of a tropical orchid is used to flavour custard and ice cream.

clue.text: Duff second degree dandy

parts.note: duff is British slang for useless; a dud is a useless thing

indicators.note: second picks out the second letter of degree

explanation.surface: A dud second-class university degree belongs to a fop.
explanation.walkthrough: DUFF is British slang for broken or useless. 'second' takes the second letter of 'degree', E.
explanation.definitionFit: A dude is a man overly concerned with his clothes, an old-fashioned fop.

clue.text: From importunate version of variation

indicators.note: a version of the word importunate is its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A pushy approach yields a slightly different take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' is a link; 'version of' rearranges the letters of IMPORTUNATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A permutation is one of the possible arrangements of a set, a variation on it.
